acceptanceCriteria: Establish the stderr resource boundary with a controlled bounded reproduction, retaining runtime evidence or explicit non-reproduction.
If needed, cap stderr capture without changing PID/start representation, snapshot ownership or cleanup semantics; retain overflow as uncertainty and verify cancellation/joins.
Keep this concern separate from V1-0689 cumulative-cap evidence; do not claim existing diagnostic runs reproduced stderr exhaustion.
body: Source-confirmed suspected resource risk, runtime NOT_RUN. At public32aa5a3f2b7f3fe658d208049fb009e2c9e24c13 internal/procgroup/descendants_posix.go:23-24 binds ps stderr to bytes.Buffer with no byte cap, while stdout uses a4MiB bounded capture. This is not an observed exhaustion or cause of V1-0689 cumulative-map failure. Expected: deliberately bounded stderr collection with explicit failure/overflow evidence, or documented evidence that the existing boundary suffices. Actual source has no stderr byte limit. Reproduce later with a controlled noisy-stderr fixture at the collection boundary; no real ps malfunction or attack reproduced here. Found in independent GateA S1 report /private/tmp/corvint-0689-independent-gate-a.md. Core1.0.0-rc.1 build163; Tasks build202. Deferred from V1-0689 repair; no additional repair prerequisite, tests or implementation authorized. Dedup searches stderr(24) and descendant(26) found no matching owning concern.
title: Investigate unbounded stderr capture in descendant process snapshots
